October 2018 – October 2022Waterton Canyon, Colorado

Waterton Canyon, CO

memories below

Right of Way

One clear October morning in 2018, on a visit back to Colorado, the road in front of me belonged to a herd of bighorn sheep. They had claimed the gravel in what I'm fairly sure was Waterton Canyon, southwest of Denver. Rams lined up along the road in a slow procession, curled horns swinging and pale rump patches flashing, while ewes grazed the golden grass beside them and rabbitbrush blazed yellow along the verge. It was probably the start of rut season, when rams settle who is boss by charging and crashing their horns together, and I caught one pair mid-argument while the rest kept right on eating. Nobody was in any hurry to move.

I came back in June 2022 and the canyon had traded its autumn straw for green. A wide, low dam spilled a white veil of water across the river, and farther along the current slowed into a calm green pool beside the dirt road, under steep rock walls and puffy clouds above the rim. One bighorn ewe stood among the shrubs by the road, her coat patchy, as if she were partway through shedding her winter wool, and watched me with total calm.

By October the canyon had turned to gold again. The sheep were back on the hillsides, grazing above a big water pipeline and its railed catwalk as if neither were there. Farther along, cottonwoods glowed yellow beside the river and patches of orange climbed the slopes, and the water broke into white rapids before settling into a still pool, with powerlines draped across the gorge overhead. Water for Denver flows through here, so it is very much a working canyon: a dam, pipes and wires threaded through it, and the sheep simply carry on. I find that comforting. A short drive from the suburbs there is still a road where the locals have priority, and I'm happy to yield.
